body:
Headaches have many causes, and for some people the neck plays a part. Understanding the difference matters, because the right approach depends on what is driving your symptoms.

## Not every headache is the same

Common headache types include tension-type headaches, migraine and headaches that seem linked to the neck, sometimes called cervicogenic headaches. They can overlap, and it is not always obvious which one you are dealing with, which is why a careful assessment is useful.

## Signs the neck may be involved

A neck contribution is more likely when headaches are felt together with neck stiffness or discomfort, and when certain movements or sustained positions seem to bring them on.

- Headaches that start at the back of the head or neck
- Symptoms that change with neck movement or posture
- Stiffness or reduced movement in the neck
- Headaches after long periods at a desk or screen

## What an assessment looks at

A physiotherapy assessment usually involves talking through your headache pattern, then looking at how your neck and upper back move, how the surrounding muscles feel and how your posture and daily habits may play a role. The aim is to work out whether musculoskeletal factors are contributing and what could help.

## What can help

Where the neck is involved, a plan may include advice on positions and habits, targeted exercises for mobility and strength, and other treatment where appropriate. Many people also benefit from looking at sleep, stress and screen breaks. If your assessment suggests another cause, you can be advised to speak to your GP.

## Key points

- Some headaches are linked to the neck, but not all
- Assessment helps separate the causes
- Exercise and habit changes are often part of the plan

## When to seek help

Seek urgent medical help for a sudden, severe headache that feels unlike any before, or a headache with fever and a stiff neck, confusion, weakness, vision changes, or after a head injury. Call 999 or NHS 111.

This article is general information and is not a substitute for an individual assessment or medical advice.
